Multiply a grayscale image by a specified colour

multiply_by_colour.Rd

Takes a grayscale image and multiplies it by a specified colour, with the option to modulate the brightness.

Usage

multiply_by_colour(img_gray, colour_hex = "#FFFFFF", brightness = 100)

Arguments

img_gray

image object. A grayscale image, e.g. produced by magick::image_read(), to be tinted the given colour.

colour_hex

character. A hex code e.g. #FF0000 to recolour the grayscale image. Default #FFFFFF (white) will not change the image. Colour keywords e.g. "red" can work, but magick uses a different library of keywords (W3C) compared to RStudio preview colours (X11), so preview colours may not match the actual output colour. In particular, "green" maps to "#00FF00" in RStudio but "#008000" in magick.

brightness

numeric. Brightness modulation to be applied to the image. 100 (default) does not alter brightness; higher values increase brightness; lower values decrease brightness.

Value

image object. The image with the specified colour tinting and brightness modulation applied.

Examples

grayscale <- image_read(system.file("extdata/images/cropped_Fus-GGC98-R.tif", package = "panelcomposite"))
#> Error in image_read(system.file("extdata/images/cropped_Fus-GGC98-R.tif",     package = "panelcomposite")): could not find function "image_read"
multiply_by_colour(grayscale, "#FF0000")
#> Error: object 'grayscale' not found
multiply_by_colour(grayscale, brightness = 200)
#> Error: object 'grayscale' not found
multiply_by_colour(grayscale, colour_hex = "#00FFFF", brightness = 50)
#> Error: object 'grayscale' not found
